messages:
nina (AE): Heads-up: Lyra's POC on Private (VPC) is hitting ~850ms first-byte for single-shot prompts. They expected <250ms. This started after we provisioned dedicated workers in their VPC region. Can we triage quickly? Also they want a ballpark committed discount for Dedicated.

jasper (SE): Which model and call pattern? Any sample logs / request ids? Are they using keepalive?

nina (AE): model=redwood-2-medium, non-streaming, client concurrency reported 4. Sample req id they gave: r-9c77b001. They also reported occasional 429s when ramping to 20 concurrent clients.

ravi (eng-oncall): grabbing traces for r-9c77b001.

infra-bot: AUTOSCALER: scale_up pool=private-vpc-lyra nodes=2 at 2025-11-04T09:12:18Z.

ravi (eng-oncall): got it. Backend trace shows: ```[2025-11-04T09:13:02Z] req=r-9c77b001 route=private-vpc-lyra batch_wait_ms=180 batch_size=1 kvcache=MISS kernel=quant_int8 first_byte_ms=843``` Min batch delay for that pool is 150ms and min_batch_size=4 by default; since many clients are single requests spaced out, runtime waits and ends up sending small batches after the delay. Also seeing kvcache MISS because nodes were replaced during scale_up -> cold cache.

jasper (SE): Two vectors: batching policy causing artificial wait + cold KV cache due to node churn. 429s when concurrency spikes likely from connection queueing or per-route concurrency guard.

ella (customer): We're running short tests and can coordinate a 30m window to try fixes. Quick question: is the KV cache persisted across pool restarts? We have compliance constraints.

jasper (SE): KV cache is in-memory on inference nodes by design for performance; not persisted to durable storage for Private deployments unless you opt into the experimental prefill service. I'll confirm with ops.

ravi (eng-oncall): Confirmed: for Lyra's private pool config KV cache is ephemeral per node and cleared on node replacement. For compliance language ping tomas.

jasper (SE): Proposed immediate mitigations for Lyra POC:
- lower pool min_batch_delay 150ms -> 10-30ms for latency sensitive workloads
- set min_batch_size=1 and enable prefer_immediate=true for the lyra route
- add a short warmup job that issues 6 concurrent tiny requests (2-5 tokens) to prefill KV on scaled nodes right after scale events
- temporarily raise route concurrency limit to absorb 20 parallel clients while we test
- recommend using keep-alive and HTTP2 to avoid TLS handshake overhead per req

nina (AE): I'll propose those and schedule a 30m window at 09:30 PT. Also Lyra asked about discounting for a 12-month reserved commit. Zoe, can sales-ops drop an L0?

zoe (sales-ops): L0 on committed pricing: provide tiered reserved discounts based on GPU-hours; for a 12mo commit we usually start at 20% off hosted list for mid-size pools and deeper for larger commits. I'll send a proper quote after usage estimate. Note: tuning min_batch_delay upward to favor latency will increase per-token unit cost slightly; include that in the quote margin.

ella (customer): We can do the 09:30 test. Is there anything we should change client-side before the window?

jasper (SE): Client-side quick wins: reuse connections, bump client concurrency to 6 for the warmup period, run warmup requests concurrently, consider disabling chunked streaming for first-byte sensitive endpoints (blocking call can be slightly faster for first byte in some workflows).

ravi (eng-oncall): I'm applying a temporary route override now: min_batch_delay=25ms min_batch_size=1 prefer_immediate=true concurrency_limit=60. Will run warmup job at 09:30:15Z.

infra-bot: ACTION: route-override applied by ravi to private-vpc-lyra at 2025-11-04T09:29:12Z.

ravi (eng-oncall): Post-change sampled trace r-9c78d2a7 -> ```[2025-11-04T09:30:22Z] req=r-9c78d2a7 batch_wait_ms=22 batch_size=1 kvcache=HIT first_byte_ms=180``` Much improved. Will continue to monitor for 15m.

ella (customer): We see ~190ms now for first byte. Great improvement. Still seeing a 429 during one spike at 09:35, suspect it was client-side burst.

nina (AE): Noted. We'll advise best-practices for client-side rate ramp (exponential ramp) and include concurrency recommendations in the POC doc.

tomas (compliance): For the questionnaire: confirmed language - KV cache is ephemeral, encrypted in transit, logging retained per contract, and customer-controlled keys available via KMS integration for control plane artifacts. I'll attach a short paragraph for you to paste into Lyra's security form.

zoe (sales-ops): I'll draft a provisional quote that includes expected ~10% uplift in unit-cost when min_batch_delay is reduced and include options for a 12mo commit.

jasper (SE): Follow-up action items: I'll write a one-page tech note summarizing latency vs batching tradeoffs and a short warmup script for customers to reuse. Nina, loop me into the customer email.

nina (AE): Thanks everyone. Ella, we'll follow up after the 30m run with results and the quote. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

ella (customer): Thanks team, this was fast and helpful.
